You have at least 10 years of hands-on design experience. Thirty is not too many.

-
You have a network among designers you respect, and you're comfortable writing to someone you admire and presenting them with an opportunity.

-
You know what the design community wants to see, and what it needs to learn.

-
You're kind, and you have the social intelligence and empathy to engage well with very different kinds of people. Much of this job is convincing busy, accomplished people that what we're building is worth their time.

-
You can show us something you built or led: a product, a design team, a course, an AI teaching app, or a conference track. We're excited to hear what it was, your thinking behind it, how long it took you to create, what went wrong, and how you improved it.

-
You can take a broad, complex design practice and turn it into a step-by-step learning sequence that'll make a beginner feel and act confident. You can look at a plan for teaching something and see what's missing before anyone builds it.

-
You're a practical idealist. You know how to create great results through incremental quick wins and MVPs, and you know when to go all in and make something perfect.

-
You’re a forward thinker who isn’t afraid to innovate and try new things before others have.

-
You collaborate with AI in everything you do. You use AI to research, structure, write, and create faster, and you know how to take human leadership, so the outcome is 100% yours and better than you could have created without AI.

-
You’re eager to help people build UX and UI skills because you know they’re more relevant than ever in the age of AI.

-
You can teach a career changer the powerful skills of great design, and you can guide an experienced designer in upskilling. Perhaps you've mentored people, or you’ve run your own company helping clients level up.

-
You give constructive feedback people can act on, and you can tell a talented colleague how they can improve their work without them becoming defensive.

-
You're genuinely curious about how AI is changing design work and design education.

-
You're fluent in written and spoken English and you can explain complex ideas clearly.

-
You’re enthusiastic about learning by doing and are committed to putting in the effort to continuously improve your skills.

-
You spot problems before anyone else notices them, and when something goes off track you come back with a solution rather than a report.

-
You value teamwork, prioritize collaboration, and focus on collective goals and harmony in the workplace.

-
You're self-motivated, and you love creative freedom, independent judgment, and the responsibility that comes with both.

-
You’re driven by the desire to make a positive impact in the world and to improve the lives of others.

-

-
Most of the work happens from your home office, but you're willing to travel a few times a year to shoot courses.

-
You're located in a time zone between UTC-6 (Austin, Chicago) and UTC+8 (Singapore, Perth), which includes all of Europe.

None of these are required, but each of them would make us even happier.

-
You've led a design team.

-
You publish your own thinking on design: articles, a book, educational material, a blog, or a social media presence.

-
You've spoken at design conferences, or you're on a first-name basis with people who do.

-
You've created design systems. Organizing complex material so other people can put it to use is a lot of what you'll be doing.

-
You've worked as an editor, or you've created online courses.

-
You have the graphic design skills to create image-based and interactive content for courses, articles, and social media.

-
You've built AI-supported learning tools yourself, or you've used AI to build products.

-
You hold a bachelor's or master's degree in UX, UI, HCI, AI, or a similar field.

-
You’ve collaborated with video production teams.

-
A highly valued role: You'll shape our core product, our courses and Master Classes.

-
Reach and impact that are difficult to find anywhere else in this field. A design leader might shape the work of thirty people on their team. Your decisions about what we teach will reach hundreds of thousands. They'll build better careers and design a better world for all of us.

-
Access: the designers you'd normally see on a conference stage are the people you'll email, plan with, and sit across from in a studio. Our name opens doors. An email from IxDF gets read, so the reach you have now is the floor, not the ceiling.

-
Autonomy: Nobody will ever hand you a template and tell you to fill it in.

-
A global, purpose-driven team: work remotely alongside passionate professionals from all over the world, united by a common mission to create the best possible design and AI education in the world and make it accessible for everyone.

-

-
A full-time position within a fully remote organization. Video-based collaboration with your colleagues from elsewhere on the planet, and we get together in person each year, on a team trip or for a studio production.

-
Bi-weekly knowledge-sharing sessions and 4 meeting-free days weekly for focused work.

-
A work culture with no fluffy titles, political agendas, or corporate drama. Your colleagues value your warm character, your strong work ethic, and the results you deliver. If you embody old-school virtues of always striving to deliver results, learn and become better every day, you'll thrive at IxDF.

-
A daily mission to help impact, empower, and enrich the lives of millions of people by creating affordable high-end design education for everyone across the planet. It'll be yours too.

-
Colleagues with four to forty years of experience, and a culture where we follow the best idea, not the longest résumé.

-
A company where the distance between idea and execution is minimal. We're a highly agile organization with zero bureaucracy or corporate politics – and with exceptional order and efficiency.

-
A company culture where passion meets high performance and excellence. To help us improve the world, and yourself in the process, you'll need grit, strong work ethic, long-term thinking, and self-discipline.

-
We thrive because we have a hands-on attitude and a bias towards action as opposed to fluff-filled, unrealistic strategies. You'll need crisp execution skills yourself and the ability to impress your colleagues with concrete results, just like they'll impress you.

-
We built online design education before people believed in it. AI is now changing what designers do, and they carry a bigger responsibility than ever. You'll be at the forefront of teaching designers to work with AI and to design responsibly for it. You'll help set a direction that shapes both the designers we teach and the people who use what they build. Together, we'll design a better world.

How to Learn More and Apply

To submit your application as well as learn more about our Work Culture and Values, please visit https://ixdf.org/about/careers

Please apply as soon as you can. We’re firm believers in “the sooner, the better” and we look forward to working with you!

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/ixdf-interaction-design-foundation-course-director-ux-ui-and-ai

jobs.title: Course Writer and Editor: UX, UI, and AI
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Denmark

URL: https://ixdf.org/about/careers

You're the one people trust with the words, whether you're writing them or fixing them. You noticed that you loved it, and that you were unusually good at it. You turn rough, complex ideas into words people understand.

Now you get the opportunity to work with some of the most respected designers alive, and help share their knowledge with hundreds of thousands of learners around the world.

A great hook pulls your readers in, makes them see themselves in the topic, and shows them why it matters in their lives. That's your craft. Abstract ideas don't stay abstract for long, because you find the example that makes an idea concrete. You're structured and systematic, yet creative, and you'll rewrite a sentence six times until it says exactly what you mean.

You see the fear around AI, and you understand where it comes from. But you also see the opportunities, and you want to show people how to work with AI in a way that benefits their lives, their users, and the world.

If you're also curious about how great design and the responsible use of AI improve people's lives, read on. As one of our Course Writers and Editors, you'll shape how our courses and Master Classes read and flow.

The industry leaders whose expertise you'll be turning into courses and Master Classes include Don Norman and Vitaly Friedman, as well as Design Leads at Netflix, LinkedIn, Meta, and Adobe.

You’ll be involved in all stages of course and Master Class creation, including key decisions, so there are incredible opportunities for you to take initiative, make meaningful contributions, and grow. Forget political struggles or long, pointless debates. You’ll be in a team with minimal distance between word and action, where decisions are made ultra-fast.

Join the Global Leader in Online Design and AI Education
IxDF is the world's largest online design and AI education platform, with over 1,150,000 enrollments since 2002. We hold the trust of industry giants like Adobe, NASA, and IBM, who rely on our courses to train their teams. Prestigious universities, including MIT and the University of Cambridge, integrate our material into their curricula. Help us take online education to new heights and make a meaningful impact on humankind.

At IxDF, we’re not just a company but a movement dedicated to making high-quality design and AI education accessible to everyone, everywhere.

We've pioneered online design education since 2002. We have over 1,150,000 enrollments and 1,583 company members, with more than 40 courses, 160 Master Classes, and thousands of open-source design resources, created by our team in collaboration with 240 industry leaders.

With learners from over 100 countries, your work will empower people worldwide.

We're Hiring Three People for Our Editorial Team
We're growing, and three roles are open at the same time to build the next generation of our core educational product. Here's what each role leads on:

-
Our Course Writers and Editors: lead how our courses and articles read. You make each title engaging, ensure each sentence flows, and edit the written course experience from the user’s perspective. This is the role described here.

-
Our Education Designers, UX, UI, and AI: lead how design and AI are taught. You plan, structure, and create the core content, and you decide what a course participant should be able to do by the end and how they get there.

-
Our Course Directors, UX, UI, and AI: lead what we teach and who teaches our courses and Master Classes. You reach out to industry leaders and create the invitation they say yes to. You bring your judgment to a planned course outline: what's missing, what doesn't belong, and whether the structure is solid. You plan and shoot courses with our Education Designers.

We’re a flexible team, and you’ll be able to do what you excel in. Everyone on our team creates courses, and everyone works across these roles. If you're torn between two roles, apply for the one you'd be best at, and tell us in your application which other one you considered and why.

You, the Course Writer and Editor, own how our courses and Master Classes read: the scripts, hooks, headings, on-screen text in videos, quiz wording, and editorial voice across everything we publish. Our Education Designers hand you the structure and the exercises, and they'll often hand you draft headings and hooks along with them. The final wording is yours. You'll work closely with our Co-Founder, your Team Lead, the Education Designers, and the Course Directors, and you'll have a real say in what we make. You'll also work closely with the video team and our growth team.

Your Role at IxDF

-
Be a core part of our Editorial Team. You'll collaborate with IxDF editors, video editors, and UX and UI designers as well as external industry leaders to create educational content for people worldwide. You'll help them succeed in the age of AI with skills in timeless, human-centered design and AI.

-
Make an impact as you decide how every course sounds. The title people want to click, the first paragraph that hooks them, the on-screen words that make our learners remember and apply what our experts teach. Our Education Designers create the structure and draft the headings, hooks, and quizzes. You finalize the scripts, hooks, headings, quiz wording, and editorial voice across everything we publish, and you give proactive feedback on the structure.

-
You don't need a design background. Most of our writers and editors start without one, and that can be an advantage because you're coming to design the way many of our learners do. In your first year you'll learn it from the inside, working through it sentence by sentence with the people who teach it, until you know what a course participant needs.

-
Write for a diverse, global audience. Some of our courses and Master Classes serve experienced designers who want to grow into more senior work. Others serve people moving into design from other fields, and many are not reading in their first language. Often, you'll write for all of them at the same time. Getting that balance right without watering anything down is a rewarding editorial challenge.

-
Be the voice of IxDF. Our reputation lives in every sentence we publish, and many of those sentences will be yours. Represent a global movement dedicated to design education, and take pride in it. It's a big responsibility, and a rewarding one.

-
Set and raise the standard for our assessments, so a correct answer proves understanding, not just recognition, and a good question teaches as well as tests. Our Education Designers decide what a question has to test. You write the wording that does both.

-
Balance the big picture with the smaller details. Expect to focus on one large course creation project per month, alongside small, continuous improvements to what's already published. You'll also write and edit articles, course descriptions, and supporting material, and help our Growth team and our two founders get the voice right in campaigns and social copy.

-
Turn expert material into lessons. Once you've built an understanding of design, you'll take a one-hour Master Class transcript and the learning goals for what the lesson must teach, then turn the strongest sections into a finished lesson. We produce 3 Master Classes per month, so new expert material arrives continuously.

-
Our courses combine written and video lessons. You'll work closely with the video team, giving constructive feedback on on-screen text, b-roll, graphics, and animation, and telling them which takeaways need a visual, so each video is more engaging to learn from.

-
Find room for improvement by looking at completion rates, learner feedback, and the portfolios learners produce, then go back and fix what isn't excellent yet. Small, incremental edits are why our material surpasses even the very best in industry and academia. We're always learning, always improving, always raising the bar in everything we do.

-
We’re committed to excellence, and we seek a like-minded enthusiast to join us. This role is not for the average. Ahead of you is a highly rewarding and enriching journey.

-
Maintain and improve our crystal-clear documentation so our knowledge resources stay up-to-date, easy to find, and provide instant value to our internal teams. Clarity is key. Any line of documentation should be self-explanatory.

-
You won't do this alone. You'll work with our Education Designers, Course Directors, your Team Lead, and our Co-Founder to pressure-test the material: you'll add what's missing, delete what's redundant, and suggest how to improve the structure. You'll be working with people who have anything from 4 to 40 years of design experience, ready to share their knowledge. We'll also help you upskill so you can grow a designer's eye alongside your editor's ear. You'll work in a diverse, highly organized, result-driven environment where you'll develop personally and professionally.

-
We're proud to have assembled a remarkable team of unicorns who uplift, motivate, and push each other to excel daily. There's a seat open for someone who shares our passion for excellence. Could that be you?

Do You Share IxDF's Vision?
People don't just buy our courses; they invest in a better version of themselves and a career they truly love. That's why every course we create and every sentence we write must do more than just inform. It must reflect the high-quality research and hands-on skills we teach.

-
Show the dream outcome: Help people imagine a future of creative, meaningful work, fulfillment, and impact through a career in design and AI.

-
Strengthen belief in success: Build confidence through real stories, practical case studies, and hands-on templates.

-
Overcome barriers: Write in a way that's crystal clear, human, and motivating. Connect and lead the way.

You'll educate, inspire, energize, and support. Whether you write a course article or give editorial feedback on a video, you'll help designers thrive in the age of AI.

About You

-
You have at least 4 years of professional writing or editing experience.

-
What matters far more than the number is the quality of the work you can show us: a course, an article series, a set of scripts, documentation, a newsletter. We’re excited to hear what it was, why you wrote it the way you did, and how long it took you to create.

-
You're a master communicator with a sharp eye for detail and strong skills in language, tone, and flow.

-
You can take a complex idea and write it so a beginner gets it on the first read.

-
You know how to hook someone with a title and a first line, and you know the difference between a hook that's earned and a hook that's cheap.

-
You collaborate with AI in everything you do. You use AI to write, research, and create faster, and you know how to take human leadership, so the outcome is 100% yours and better than you could have created without AI.

-
You’re eager to help people build UX and UI skills because you know they’re more relevant than ever in the age of AI.

-
You can write for a career changer and for an experienced designer without losing either one.

-
You have an exceptional talent for creating structure, and you take pride in organizing processes and tasks in a way that's efficient and clear.

-
You're genuinely curious about UX and UI design, and you're motivated to learn how great design shapes experiences and solves problems.

-
You're genuinely curious about how AI is changing design work and design education, and you look for new ways to use it in your own work.

-
You're kind, and you have the social intelligence and empathy to engage well with very different kinds of people.

-
You're fluent in written and spoken English, your grammar is exact, and you understand the power of tone, brevity, and microcopy.

-
You take full ownership of your work and see it through. You move comfortably across ad hoc projects of varying complexity, and you stay consistent when the work turns repetitive.

-
You’re enthusiastic about learning by doing and are committed to putting in the effort to continuously improve your skills.

-
You spot problems before anyone else notices them, and when something goes off track you come back with a solution rather than a report.

-
You value teamwork, prioritize collaboration, and focus on collective goals and harmony in the workplace.

-
You work well with great responsibility and freedom inside a well-documented, structured system. Accuracy and attention to detail are key on an online learning platform, where every tag must be correct and every piece of text formatted to our upload system. It's in your nature to meticulously double-check that everything is in order.

-
You're self-motivated, and you love creative freedom, independent judgment, and the responsibility that comes with both.

-
You’re driven by the desire to make a positive impact in the world and to improve the lives of others.

-
You're located in a time zone between UTC+0 (London) and UTC+4 (Dubai), which covers Europe, the Middle East, and Africa.

Bonus Points
None of these are required, but each of them would make us even happier.

-
You've taught in classrooms or workshops, or you've created educational material.

-
You have your own blog or social media page where you create and share original content.

-
You’ve collaborated with video production teams.

-
You've written quiz or assessment questions.

-
You've worked with an LMS or an online learning platform.

-
You hold a bachelor's or master's degree in communications, journalism, literature, or a similar field.

What We Can Offer

-
A highly valued role: You'll shape our core product, our courses and Master Classes.

-
Reach and impact that are difficult to find anywhere else in this field. Your words will be read year after year, by hundreds of thousands of people who build better careers and design a better world for all of us. An education you can't buy: free access to every IxDF course and Master Class, and a job that requires you to study the work of the best designers alive in order to edit it. Most people pay for this. You'll be paid for it.

-
Access: the designers whose books you'd normally buy are the people whose words you'll be shaping, and in some cases the people you'll be in a studio with.

-
Studio shoots: once you know our courses well, usually after your first year, you'll be a real asset on a studio production, and you'll be welcome to join us when we meet our experts in professional studios around the world. Some of us love that part and go every time; others keep travel to a minimum. Both work for us. On average we shoot 4-6 new courses per year.

-
Autonomy: Nobody will ever hand you a template and tell you to fill it in. You decide how our courses read.

-
A global, purpose-driven team: Work remotely alongside passionate professionals from all over the world, united by a common mission to create the best possible design and AI education in the world and make it accessible for everyone.

-
Our co-founder and co-CEO, Rikke, will work closely with you. She and our other co-founder, Mads, built IxDF from nothing, with no investment capital, so we would stay free to make world-class design education affordable to everyone. She was the sole editor and video editor for many of our early years, so she's shaped our course planning, expert interviews, video shoots, and content editing from the inside. She's still hands-on in everything we do, and she still films educational videos herself, in places like the US, the North Pole, and Nepal.

-
A full-time position within a fully remote organization. Video-based collaboration with your colleagues from elsewhere on the planet, and we get together in person each year, on a team trip or a studio production.

-
Bi-weekly knowledge-sharing sessions and 4 meeting-free days weekly for focused work.

-
A work culture with no fluffy titles, political agendas, or corporate drama. Your colleagues value your warm character, your strong work ethic, and the results you deliver. If you embody old-school virtues of always striving to deliver results, learn and become better every day, you'll thrive at IxDF.

-
A daily mission to help impact, empower, and enrich the lives of millions of people by creating affordable high-end design education for everyone across the planet. It'll be yours too.

-
A company where the distance between idea and execution is minimal. We're a highly agile organization with zero bureaucracy or corporate politics – and with exceptional order and efficiency.

-
A company culture where passion meets high performance and excellence. To help us improve the world, and yourself in the process, you'll need grit, strong work ethic, long-term thinking, and self-discipline.

-
We thrive because we have a hands-on attitude and a bias towards action as opposed to fluff-filled, unrealistic strategies. You'll need crisp execution skills yourself and the ability to impress your colleagues with concrete results, just like they'll impress you.

-
If you want even more opportunities to show the world what you can do, you’re in luck! When you're willing to do the hard work of learning and growing, then you’ll find virtually limitless opportunities with us.

-
We built online design education before people believed in it. AI is now changing what designers do, and they carry a bigger responsibility than ever. You'll be at the forefront of teaching designers to work with AI and to design responsibly for it. You'll help set a direction that shapes both the designers we teach and the people who use what they build. Together, we'll design a better world.

How to Learn More and Apply

To submit your application as well as learn more about our Work Culture and Values, please visit https://ixdf.org/about/careers

Please apply as soon as you can. We’re firm believers in “the sooner, the better” and we look forward to working with you!

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/ixdf-interaction-design-foundation-course-writer-and-editor-ux-ui-and-ai

Headquarters: Remote, US

Description

Keeper is hiring a driven SLED (state, local, and higher education) focused Associate Account Manager to join a high producing team within our B2B sales division. This is a 100% remote position from select locations, with an opportunity to work a hybrid schedule for candidates who live near our global headquarters in Chicago.

Keeper’s cybersecurity software is trusted by millions of people and thousands of organizations, globally. Keeper is published in 23 languages and is sold in over 150 countries. Join one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity companies and gain valuable skills while expanding and developing client relationships in this pivotal role!

About Keeper Security

Keeper Security is a leading cybersecurity software company that protects thousands of organizations and millions of people in more than 150 countries. Keeper delivers a powerful zero-trust and zero-knowledge solution built to meet the stringent requirements of state, local and educational (SLED) IT environments. Its flagship offering, KeeperPAM®, is an AI-enabled, cloud-native platform that protects users, devices and critical infrastructure from cyber attacks. Recognized in the Gartner® Magic QuadrantTM for Privileged Access Management (PAM), Keeper combines robust compliance with unmatched visibility and control. With industry-leading certifications, including GovRAMP Authorization, Keeper provides the security assurance public sector organizations require. Learn why agencies trust Keeper to defend against today’s sophisticated adversaries at KeeperSecurity.com.

About the Role

Join an elite group of proven performers and highly successful Associate Account Manager professionals. Our team is full of seasoned technologists, with experience selling into SME and Enterprise level accounts. They have a passion for helping companies get the most out of their technology investments and are skilled at identifying new business opportunities and expansion opportunities within named accounts. As a SLED focused Associate Account Manager, you will work with an established client base within the public sector, concentrating on state, local, and higher education and be responsible for growing revenue through these accounts using our industry-leading solutions.

Responsibilities

- Thrive in a supportive but independent workplace with the opportunity to grow as our organization grows
- Carry a revenue quota to meet or exceed sales targets within assigned accounts
- Provide strong interactions with customers at the Senior Management level with support on forming relationships with C level contacts
- Work with clients to negotiate contract renewals, cross-sells and upsells
- Work with clients to establish business and technical goals & potential via technical and Quarterly Business Reviews
- Navigate SLED-specific procurement processes, including RFP/RFI responses, contract vehicles, cooperative purchasing agreements, and compliance requirements (e.g., FedRAMP, StateRAMP, CJIS, etc.)
- Build and manage relationships with key public sector stakeholders, including government agencies, educational institutions, and internal champions, aligning Keeper solutions with mission-driven objectives and budget cycles
- Understand public sector funding models and budget timelines to effectively position renewals, expansions, and multi-year agreements
- Maintain a structured cadence with named customer accounts, build relationships, present Keeper solutions, troubleshoot challenges, manage issues with the broader Keeper team and close deals
- Advise customers on best practices for securing and protecting their business against password related breaches
- Proactively manage the success of a portfolio of assigned Keeper Security customers to deliver consistent value across the entire lifecycle
- Consistently demonstrate knowledge of Account Management best practices, stay up to date on trends in the industry, and operate as an Account Manager and Cybersecurity advisor to your customers
- Understand and navigate account procurement practices to negotiate licensing contracts
- Resolve customer issues, alone and through collaboration with other Keeper Security teams; approach all situations with curiosity and creativity. Resolving customer issues can involve troubleshooting and require deep technical knowledge of our solutions and the Password management space
- Build strong customer relationships by maintaining high levels of engagement, adoption, and communication; conduct quarterly business reviews to ensure our clients are up to speed on their areas of vulnerability, new product features etc.
- Become a Keeper Security product expert for your customers; occasionally assist on Sales or Marketing calls/webinars as an Account Manager & Keeper expert
- Drive customer advocacy in the form of references, referrals, and case studies
- Perform data-driven reviews and analysis on customer portfolio to prioritize opportunity and risk; reliably renew and expand customer contracts, meet and exceed personal and team quotas
- Participate in the evolution of Keeper Security’s own Account Management programs and processes; insist on excellence in our own AM initiatives
- Contribute towards the development of a strong team environment by upholding high work standards
- Jump at opportunities to go the extra mile to ensure our customers are supported and successful!

Requirements

- 2+ years of experience within software or tech sales (with a focus on upselling and expansion)
- 1+ years of SLED or government sales experience within software or tech sales
- Strong technical knowledge as it pertains to software integrations (SSO, Directory etc), implementation, onboarding & support
- Experience working in IAM or cybersecurity industry
- Motivated by solving problems for customers; demonstrated ability to anticipate challenges before they arise
- Experience working with and selling to Enterprise organizations, IT and Cyber Security Executives
- Unrivaled sense of autonomy, ownership, and dedication to helping customers realize their intended value
- Energetic and self-motivated; a team player who is also a proactive and creative problem solver
- Aptitude for learning software; strong with business applications
- Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining strict attention to details. Strong communication and interpersonal skills, both written and verbal; consistent diplomacy, tact, and poise when working through customer issues and escalations
- Working knowledge of Salesforce.com
- Undergraduate degree preferred (BA/BS)

Benefits

- Medical, Dental & Vision (Inclusive of domestic partnerships)
- Employer Paid Life Insurance & Employee/Spouse/Child Supplemental life
- Voluntary Short/Long Term Disability Insurance
- 401k (Roth/Traditional)
- A generous PTO plan that celebrates your commitment and seniority (including paid Bereavement/Jury Duty, etc)

Keeper Security, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer and participant in the U.S. Federal

E-Verify program. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Classification: Non-Exempt

Keeper Candidate Privacy Notice

This notice explains how Keeper Security processes your personal data during recruitment. Depending on the role and location, the Controller of personal data (the organization responsible for determining why and how personal data is processed) will be Keeper Security Inc. (US), Keeper Security EMEA Ltd. (Ireland), or Keeper Security APAC K.K (Japan).

 1. Data We Collect

Information You provide:

Contact details, CV/resume, cover letter
Employment history, qualifications, work eligibility
Application responses and uploaded documents

Information We generate:

Interview notes, assessments, communications
Scheduling information

Information From Others:

Recruiter/referral information who submit your profile
References (with your consent, before final offer)
Public professional profiles
Background verification (post offer)

 Voluntary Diversity and Equal Opportunity Information

We may ask you to voluntarily provide diversity information including race/ethnicity, gender, disability status and veteran status (US). Providing this information is optional and Keeper collects this data in order to comply with EEOC and similar requirements

 2. How We Use Your Data

Assess your application and suitability
Manage interviews and recruitment workflow
Consider you for other/future roles (we may seek your consent to keep your information on our systems beyond the retention period specified)
Comply with employment law obligations

 3. Legal Basis

Legitimate Interests (recruitment management, security and integrity of the hiring process)
Contracting steps (for progressed candidates)
Legal and regulatory compliance obligations; explicit consent where required

 4. Who We Share Information With

Internal:

HR, hiring managers, interviewers*, IT support for system administration

*Note - diversity and equal opportunity data is not shared with hiring managers.

Third Parties:

Service providers who assist with:

Applicant tracking, recruitment systems and assessment providers
Background verification vendors (post offer)
Recruitment agencies (where applicable)
Tools to support communication, collaboration and to securely store your data

Keeper ensures that all our third parties are contractually bound to protect your personal data with adequate safeguards in place.

 5. International Transfers

Your data may be accessed by Keeper entities globally as needed for the purposes of hiring and decision making. We protect any such data transfer between Keeper entities using appropriate safeguards under applicable data protection laws.

6. Security

We implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect your data, consistent with our industry leading security standards.

7. Retention

We keep your data for 24 months from your last application activity, then delete or anonymize it.

Exceptions:

You opt into our talent database for further retention by providing consent (extended retention)
You're hired (transfers to employee records)

 8. Your Rights

You have the following rights and can contact us at the email below to exercise them:

Access, correct, or delete your data, subject to applicable law and retention requirements
Object to or restrict processing
Withdraw consent (where applicable)
Request data portability
Lodge a complaint with your data protection authority

If you become an employee, your rights regarding your employee record are governed by our internal Employee Privacy Notice and certain data will be retained as required under relevant laws such as employment or tax law.

When you request access to your personal data, some information may be redacted if it includes the personal data of other individuals or information that we must protect in order to preserve their privacy rights.

 9. Automated Decisions

Keeper does not make hiring decisions using solely automated processing.

10. Contact - Candidates can send privacy questions to: privacy@keepersecurity.com

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer II Full Stack - Business (Remote @ Colombia)
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote @ Colombia

About the role:

The OfferUp Business team owns the platforms that power every business vertical on our marketplace; Storefronts, Auto Dealers, Services, Rentals, and Jobs. Our customers aren't casually browsing; they're running businesses on top of what we build, so every feature we ship has a direct, measurable impact on their livelihood and on OfferUp's revenue. We operate the full stack end-to-end: including microservices that handle some of the highest RPS and TPS in the company, and integrations with partners like Stripe and Shopify. We move fast, instrument everything, and treat experimentation as a first-class part of the workflow. We've barely scratched the surface of what these verticals can become, and the roadmap is wide open for someone who wants to help shape it.

At many organizations, your role begins and ends with the code. On our team, we’re different. You own a feature from concept to fruition. Your responsibilities will include everything from writing well architected and thoroughly tested code, to rolling out the feature by analyzing metrics. You also get to take ownership beyond your technical area by working with cross-functional team members.

As a Full Stack Software Engineer II on the Business team, you'll be a proven contributor who ships features end-to-end across the stack. From the React components our business customers interact with, to the Java services and data pipelines behind them. You'll take real ownership of the work you deliver, raise the quality of the code around you, and grow into a high-performing, reliable contributor on the team.

Here’s more of what you will get to do:

- Design, build, and deploy new user experiences and backend services across our five business verticals, using React, TypeScript, GraphQL, Node.js, and Java
- Own features end-to-end: plan, design, develop, deploy, measure, and iterate
- Break down complex engineering problems into achievable tasks and deliver them within committed timeframes
- Work collaboratively with cross-functional teams (Product, Design, Data, Business stakeholders) to design and implement new features
- Contribute to A/B tests and use experimentation results to decide what ships
- Actively participate in code reviews and enforce good patterns, testing, and edge-case handling
- Coach and mentor junior team members, new hires, and interns
- Create shared components, utilities, and services that improve team velocity across the stack
- Maintain and improve the runbooks, alerting, and monitoring for the features you ship
- Participate in a reasonable on-call rotation with the rest of the team
- Use AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, and similar) to increase your daily development velocity and code quality
- Become a subject matter expert in one or more of the team's sub-domains

You’ll thrive in this role if you have:

- 2+ years of professional software engineering experience
- Demonstrated ability to own the delivery of multiple features end-to-end (plan, design, develop, and deploy) with high efficiency, including breaking down engineering problems into achievable tasks
- Strong coding skills across the full stack:

- React, TypeScript, HTML, CSS, and modern web tooling; good grasp of responsive design, performance, and cross-browser compatibility
- Java and a working understanding of microservices and distributed-systems fundamentals

- Experience building and integrating with REST or GraphQL APIs
- Good knowledge of data structures and object-oriented design
- Hands-on experience using AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, or similar) in a real engineering workflow, and a point of view on when they help and when they don't
- Follows good coding patterns, writes appropriate tests, considers trade-offs, and actively seeks out edge cases
- Comfortable giving and receiving feedback in code reviews
- A bias toward shipping, learning from production, and iterating quickly
- An insatiable desire and ability to learn
- BS or MS in Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience

Helpful, but not required:

- Fluency in any other modern OOO programming language
- Experience with Agile development
- Experience with AWS Cloud infrastructure
- Experience around any of the following: web package managers, Bower, bundler system, NodeJS, Python, webpack
- Experience with A/B testing platforms (Statsig, LaunchDarkly, Optimizely) and analytics warehouses (BigQuery, Snowflake)
- Experience consuming or integrating LLM-based APIs (e.g., Bedrock, Vertex AI, OpenAI)
- Familiarity with AWS cloud infrastructure and CI/CD pipelines
About OfferUp:

OfferUp is dedicated to creating the simplest and most trusted way for people to buy, sell, and connect in their local communities. One of the top local marketplace apps for local buyers and sellers in the U.S., OfferUp makes it easy for people to discover more of what they need—from great deals and secondhand goods to jobs, services, home rentals, and more—right in their own communities. Our trusted platform empowers millions to connect, thrive, and move life forward.

Available on iOS and Android, OfferUp has consistently ranked among the top shopping apps. Founded in 2011 and based in Bellevue, WA, OfferUp serves local markets nationwide and was used by more than 1 in 6 adults in the U.S. in 2024. OfferUp is backed by leading investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Warburg Pincus, GGV Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Coatue Management. https://about.offerup.com

More About OfferUp At a Glance

- Top 10 Shopping app in the App Store and Google Play Store for three years
- 15%+ of adults in several major markets use OfferUp every month (LA, Miami, Phoenix, Seattle, Las Vegas, Riverside, Orlando)

Typeform is a refreshingly different form builder. We help over 150,000 businesses collect the data they need with forms, surveys, and quizzes that people enjoy. You'll join a small but high-impact Accounting & Controlling team at a pivotal moment in Typeform's journey.

As we've grown into a global SaaS business, our finance function is evolving to support greater scale, complexity, and ambition. We're investing in stronger financial controls, more sophisticated accounting operations, and systems that will enable our next stage of growth.

You'll partner closely with the VP of Accounting & Controlling, serving as their strategic deputy and helping lead both the day-to-day function and the longer-term evolution of our accounting organization. As Director of Accounting & Controlling, you'll lead the operational accounting function while helping shape the future of finance at Typeform.

Reporting to the VP of Accounting & Controlling, you'll own the integrity of our global accounting operations, oversee a growing team, and drive initiatives that strengthen financial controls, improve efficiency, and support international growth. - Experience preparing an organization for rapid international growth, acquisitions, or IPO readiness

While a traditional allogeneic stem cell transplant has been the best hope for many, the transplant itself can prove fatal or lead to serious conditions, such as graft vs. host disease. jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer Case Execution
jobs.description:
About Pivotal HealthPivotal Health is the leading technology platform that helps healthcare providers get paid fairly in an increasingly complex reimbursement landscape.

Today, many providers face persistent underpayment from health insurance companies, despite delivering high-quality care. While processes like IDR (Independent Dispute Resolution) were designed to promote fairness, theyâre often administrative-heavy, time-consuming, and difficult to navigate without the right tools.

Pivotal Health combines software, data, and service into a seamlessly integrated, AI-driven platform that simplifies these complex reimbursement workflows. We help providers efficiently dispute underpaid claims, reduce administrative burden, and recover the reimbursement theyâre entitled to; without adding more work to already stretched teams.

Our full-service IDR solution is just the starting point. Weâre building solutions that enable providers to operate with clarity, control, and confidence across the reimbursement journey.

About the RoleWe're hiring a Senior Software Engineer to join Pivotal's Case Execution team. This team owns critical parts of the case execution workflow, including eligibility, batching, submissions, ops workflows, and claim orchestration. These systems sit at the operational core of how Pivotal delivers outcomes for providers.

This is a strong fit for an engineer who enjoys solving complex, workflow-driven backend problems and working through data-heavy decision logic. The most technically demanding areas for this team are eligibility and batching, and the right person is energized by that kind of work rather than looking to avoid it.

What You'll Do

- Build and improve core case execution systems: Own backend development across eligibility, batching, submissions, ops workflows, and claim orchestration.  These are the systems that determine how cases move through Pivotal's platform and reach resolution.

- Tackle complex, data-driven backend problems: Work through the decision logic and data-heavy workflows that make eligibility and batching hard, understanding not just how individual systems work, but how they interact across the broader platform.

- Contribute to workflow orchestration: Build and improve the systems that coordinate how cases are staged, routed, and executed end to end, with a clear eye toward correctness and reliability.

- Collaborate cross-functionally: Work closely with the Integrations team, Case Strategy team, and other engineering and product partners to ensure systems are well-connected and aligned with how the broader platform operates.

- Contribute to front-end and admin workflows where needed: The role is primarily backend-focused, but you'll contribute to internal-facing UI and ops tooling where the product requires it.

Who You Are

- 5+ years of software engineering experience with a strong backend focus

- Strong engineering fundamentals with hands-on experience building data-heavy, workflow-oriented systems

- Experience working on complex, data-driven decision logic or orchestration problems: you're comfortable with systems where correctness and sequencing both matter

- Comfortable operating in a collaborative, fast-moving startup environment where ownership and requirements evolve

- Python experience; able to work effectively in a Python-based backend environment

- Self-directed and proactive: you identify problems and drive them to resolution without heavy oversight

- Strong communicator who collaborates well across engineering, product, and adjacent teams

Extra Credit If You Have

- Experience with healthcare-specific data or HealthTech systems

- Exposure to data-heavy architectures or problems adjacent to data engineering without being a pure data engineer

- Familiarity with tools like Snowflake, dbt, or Databricks

- Some front-end experience to support admin workflow contributions

Why Youâll Love Working HereWeâre a collaborative, low-ego team on a mission to make healthcare reimbursement fairer for providers. While we primarily hire around our core hubsâLos Angeles and New Yorkâwe remain open to exceptional talent outside those regions. Remote and hybrid flexibility varies by role and team, and is outlined in each job description.

If youâre excited by solving complex problems and making a real-world impact, weâd love to hear from you.

Benefits Include:

- Competitive compensation, including equity

- Full health, dental, and vision coverage

- Retirement savings plan through 401(k)

- Flexible time off

- Opportunities for company-wide connection and events

Ready to Make an Impact?
Weâre building something meaningful; and we want you on the team.

Bring your ideas, curiosity, and drive, and letâs transform healthcare reimbursement together.

jobs.description:
About KIRAOur mission is to make money smart, reliable and within reach for everyone.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in Asia and it includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and at ease and self reliance, become an expert. We believe AI will help us achieve this in our generation.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future

Â The RoleWe are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a high-performing engineering team building and scaling products used by millions of users across the region.

This role is for a strong technical leader who can lead engineers, make sound architecture and engineering decisions, and drive products and systems from idea to production. You will be responsible for both the quality of the engineering team and the quality and speed of what the team ships.

You should be comfortable operating across people, product and technology â setting a high engineering bar while keeping the team focused on delivering real customer and business outcomes.

What You'll Own- Lead and manage a team of engineers across frontend, backend and full stack development.

- Own engineering delivery for major product areas, ensuring the team ships quickly without compromising reliability and technical quality.

- Work closely with product, design, mobile, backend and AI teams to turn ambiguous product problems into clear technical execution.

- Drive technical architecture and engineering decisions across APIs, databases, integrations, infrastructure and customer-facing systems.

- Set engineering standards around code quality, system design, testing, observability, security and production reliability.

- Stay close to the technical work through architecture reviews, code reviews, debugging and critical engineering decisions.

- Develop engineers through regular feedback, coaching, performance management and clear expectations.

- Identify performance gaps early and take ownership of raising the team's engineering and execution bar.

- Improve engineering processes, tooling and automation to help the team move faster and operate at scale.

- Own production outcomes beyond release: monitor systems, resolve incidents, identify root causes and ensure problems do not repeat.

- Build a strong engineering culture focused on ownership, speed, technical excellence and continuous improvement.

What We're Looking For- Strong software engineering background with experience building and shipping real production systems.

- Experience leading or managing software engineers and owning engineering delivery.

- Strong technical depth across backend, frontend, APIs, databases, distributed systems or cloud infrastructure.

- Able to make sound architecture and technical trade-offs while balancing speed, scalability and maintainability.

- Strong track record of taking products or systems from idea through development, launch and production.

- Comfortable reviewing technical designs, challenging engineering decisions and debugging complex production issues.

- Strong people leadership with the ability to coach engineers, manage performance and build high-performing teams.

- Strong product sense and ability to connect engineering decisions to customer and business outcomes.

- Able to work fast with ambiguity, establish priorities and drive teams toward clear outcomes.

- Strong ownership mentality â when something breaks or delivery slips, you take responsibility for getting it back on track.

This Role Is Not For- Managers who want to manage people without staying close to the technology.

- Engineers who want the title of Engineering Manager but do not want accountability for team performance.

- Leaders who need complete specifications before their team can start.

- Managers who measure success by meetings, processes or tickets instead of shipped outcomes.

- People who avoid difficult technical decisions, performance conversations or production issues.

- Candidates who make vague leadership claims without being able to explain what they personally built, led, improved or scaled.

The BarWe are looking for engineering leaders with real technology career highlights.

A strong highlight is not just managing a large team or working at a famous company. A strong highlight means you personally helped build, ship or scale a serious product, platform or engineering organisation and can clearly explain your contribution.

 You should be able to demonstrate both sides of engineering leadership: technical depth and the ability to build a high-performing team that consistently delivers.

LocationThis is a remote role. We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones.

Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.

Â LanguageEnglish is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview ProcessOur process is designed to move fast:

- Online assessment or practical task

- Technical / engineering leadership interview

- CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

jobs.title: Staff Brand Designer
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote

URL: https://webflow.com/

Webflow is the agentic web marketing platform for modern marketing teams, helping organizations build, manage, and optimize high-performing web experiences that drive predictable growth and strengthen brand trust. Building at Webflow will need grit, because we move fast, without ever sacrificing craft or quality.

We're looking for a Staff Brand Designer who works in the space between brand and web—someone who can hold a brand idea and build it themselves. Our marketing site is where most people meet Webflow, which makes it the primary surface of our brand rather than a place we put finished work. You'll design that experience and take it all the way into production on our own platform. The brand doesn't stop at the site, though—it shows up in campaigns, conference environments, film, and the product itself—and you'll work across those surfaces too. The border between those disciplines is disappearing in practice: a conference identity now ships as a motion system and a site in the same breath, and an announcement has to hold in a keynote and a viewport in the same week. This role also sits closest to the edge of what's newly possible, so we care most about someone who is already experimenting—putting AI and agentic tooling to real use and bringing back what holds up. You'll sit on Brand Studio, Webflow's in-house creative team, as a senior individual contributor working alongside brand designers, motion, and marketing partners.

About the role:

- Location: Remote-first (United States; BC & ON, Canada)
- Full-time
- Permanent
- Exempt
- The cash compensation for this role is tailored to align with the cost of labor in different geographic markets. We've structured the base pay ranges for this role into zones for our geographic markets, and the specific base pay within the range will be determined by the candidate’s geographic location, job-related experience, knowledge, qualifications, and skills.

- United States  (all figures cited below are in USD and pertain to workers in the United States)

- Zone A: $162,500 - $195,000
- Zone B: $153,300 - $184,000
- Zone C: $143,300 - $172,000

- Canada (figures cited below are in CAD and pertain to workers in ON & BC, Canada)

- 177,000 - 213,000

This role is also eligible to participate in Webflow's company-wide bonus program. Target amounts are a percentage of base salary and vary by career level. Payouts are based on company performance against established financial and operational goals.

Please visit our Careers page for more information on which locations are included in each of our geographic pay zones. However, please confirm the zone for your specific location with your recruiter.

- Application Information:

- Application deadline: applications accepted on an ongoing basis until position is closed and filled
- This posting is for an existing vacancy

- Reporting to the Manager, Brand Studio

As a Staff Brand Designer, you'll…

Design the web as our primary brand surface

- Treat webflow.com as the place most people meet the brand, and design it as an experience rather than a stack of sections.
- Shape pacing, narrative, and flow across a visitor's path, not just the layout of individual pages.
- Express the brand through behavior—type, motion, interaction, and state—not only through how a frame looks at rest.
- Extend the brand system into web-native patterns and components that other designers and marketers can use without you in the room.

Work in the space between brand and web

- Design and build in the same motion, carrying work from brand idea to shipped page without handing it off at the seam.
- Act as the primary technical owner of Webflow's marketing surface area, from CMS architecture to component systems to publishing workflow.
- Build on Webflow as our most sophisticated customer, so the site stands as proof of what the platform can do rather than an exception to it.
- Hold the craft bar on brand expression and the technical bar on implementation at the same time, and know when the two are in tension.
- Make architectural calls that balance ambition against performance, scalability, and the cost of maintaining them a year from now.
- Ship launches, campaign pages, and fixes with speed and accuracy under real deadline pressure, including moments like Webflow Conf, and own performance, accessibility, and SEO health as ongoing commitments.

Work across the brand's other surfaces

- Bring the same standard to work that isn't a website: campaign systems, conference environments, editorial, film, and the brand's expression inside the product.
- Design for coherence across surfaces, so an idea that starts on the site still holds up in a keynote, a video, or a physical space.
- Understand how a brand system has to behave differently in each medium, and help evolve the system itself rather than only its web expression.

Experiment, and put what works into production

- Work in the open with AI-assisted design and development, generative code, and agentic build tooling, and bring back what actually holds up under a quality bar.
- Explore advanced and pre-release platform capabilities and ship them ahead of the market.
- Build the experiments that make an argument—a working prototype that settles a debate faster than a deck would.
- Use generative and agentic tooling where it closes the gap between designing a system and building it, which is increasingly the same act.
- Develop the team's practice as you go, so a tool you proved out this month is something everyone is using next month.
- Feed real practitioner insight back to Product and Engineering, because you're building on the thing we sell.

Unblock the business

- Partner with Brand Studio, Product Marketing, Growth, Legal, and Events to get campaigns and launches live without compromising the site.
- Reduce dependency bottlenecks by making your expertise available early, when decisions are still cheap to change.
- Mentor designers and marketers through pairing, feedback, and the systems and guardrails you build for them.
- Translate technical constraints into plain language so non-technical partners can make good tradeoffs themselves.

In addition to the responsibilities outlined above, at Webflow we will support you in identifying where your interests and development opportunities lie and we'll help you incorporate them into your role.

About you:
Requirements:

- BS/BA college degree or relevant experience
- 8+ years of experience spanning brand design and web design or development, with work that clearly shows both
- Demonstrated experience designing marketing websites as a primary surface of a brand—narrative, flow, and interaction across a journey, not just individual page layouts
- Deep, demonstrable Webflow expertise, including complex CMS structures, components, interactions, performance work, and system-level thinking
- Experience contributing to brand work beyond websites—campaigns, environments, editorial, motion, or product surfaces—with a view on how a brand system has to change shape in each
- Active AI fluency: you are already using AI and agentic tooling in real production work, and can show what you have built with it, what you have thrown away, and how you tell those apart
- Familiarity with code: you read HTML and CSS comfortably, can follow and adapt JavaScript, and are not stuck when a build needs to go past the visual editor. Professional development experience is not required.
- A portfolio that shows both identity-level craft and shipped, high-traffic sites you can speak to at the architecture level

You’ll thrive as a Staff Brand Designer if you:

- Think about a website as an experience with pacing and narrative, rather than a set of pages to be laid out.
- Treat new tools as material to be tested rather than trends to have an opinion about, and can tell the difference between a capability and a demo.
- Move fluidly between a type-scale decision and a CMS schema decision, and consider neither beneath you nor outside your job.
- Are as interested in what the brand does in a room or a keynote as in what it does in a viewport.
- Like that the work is public evidence—people inspect how webflow.com is built to decide what the platform can do.
- Reach for a prototype before a deck, and would rather show the thing working than describe it.
- Think in systems first, and can explain why you structured something the way you did three releases later.
- Care about craft at the level of a 40ms transition and a 200-page class system in equal measure.
- Bring calm and clarity to complex, fast-moving launches, and would rather surface a risk early than absorb it quietly.
- Want meaningful technical ownership without formal people management, and get real satisfaction from scaling your impact through standards, tooling, and mentorship.
- Communicate well with people who don't share your vocabulary, and give feedback that makes work better rather than smaller.
- Have opinions about where the web is going as agents take on more of the building, and are already testing them in production.
- Stay curious and open to growth—demonstrating a proactive embrace of AI, and actively building and applying fluency in emerging technologies to elevate how we work, drive faster outcomes, and expand collective impact.

Our Core Behaviors:

- Build lasting customer trust. We build trust by taking action that puts customer trust first.
- Win together. We play to win, and we win as one team. Success at Webflow isn't a solo act.
- Reinvent ourselves. We don't just improve what exists, we imagine what's possible.
- Own it all the way. We move fast because the moment demands it, and we hold ourselves accountable to deliver outcomes — for each other, and for customers.

Benefits

- Ownership in what you help build. Every permanent Webflower receives equity (RSUs) in our growing, privately held company.
- Health coverage that actually covers you. Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans for full-time employees and their dependents, with Webflow covering most premiums.
- Support for every stage of family life. 12 weeks of paid parental leave for all parents and 6+ weeks of additional paid leave for birthing parents. Plus inclusive care for family planning, menopause, and midlife transitions.
- Time off that’s actually off. Flexible vacation, paid holidays, and a sabbatical program to help you recharge and come back inspired.
- Wellness for the whole you. Access to mental health resources, therapy and coaching.
- Invest in your future. A 401(k) with 100% employer match (up to $6,000/year) in the U.S., and support for retirement savings globally.
- Monthly stipends that flex with your life. Localized support for work and wellness expenses — from Wi-Fi to workouts.
- Bonus for building together. All full-time, permanent, non-commission employees are eligible for our annual WIN bonus program.

Remote, together
At Webflow, equality is a core tenet of our culture. We are an Equal Opportunity (EEO)/Veterans/Disabled Employer and are committed to building an inclusive global team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, beliefs, and experiences. Employment decisions are made on the basis of job-related criteria without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other classification protected by applicable law. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, Webflow will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

jobs.title: Surveyor I
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Surveyor I is an entry or junior-level position for new graduates and/or those candidates with less than five (5) years of experience in an applicable industry. The Surveyor I, under a direct supervisor, performs work involving conventional surveying practices. The primary function is to develop the ability to effectively examine and report on vessels and other marine structures during and after construction relative to compliance with the applicable requirements for maintaining the vessel in Classification with ABS and meeting associated statutory and special service requirements related to Safety of Life at Sea, Loadline, Tonnage, Cargo Gear and Pollution Prevention Certification.

What You Will Do (with the assistance and guidance of an experienced ABS Surveyor):

- Acts as a professional specialist for the organization in the application of related rules, regulations, requirements, concepts, principles, and processes. - Performs routine surveys on classed vessels, platforms, or other marine structures and at manufacturers for classification and compliance with statutory requirements. - Prepares technically accurate and timely reports of inspections and surveys performed. - Engages in contact with clients to resolve problems within areas of expertise. - Maintains survey files in an orderly and up-to-date manner in the area of responsibility. - Develops the skills necessary for the administration of office procedures and monitoring of business performance at an assigned port. - Through broader and more technically challenging work assignments, the individual must develop a thorough understanding of field operations, policies, methods, and procedures.

What You Will Need:

Education and Experience

- Qualifications from a tertiary institution within a relevant field of engineering or physical science (minimum two (2) years program); or- Qualifications from a marine or nautical institution and relevant seagoing experience as a certificated ship officer, and- Proficiency in the English language commensurate with the scope of statutory certification and services and, before assignment, with their future work. - Appropriate certification and/or licenses in areas of specialization may be required.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

- Ability to develop a working knowledge of ABS Rules, Guides, statutory regulations, and related instructions, as well as the ABS Employee Safety Policy. - Ability to read engineering plans and have a basic understanding of shipbuilding practices and vessel operations. - Ability to perform surveys in the prescribed format. - Knowledge of computer programs or software packages related to job responsibilities. - Knowledge of related technical interfaces required for group project work. - Knowledge of ships' engineering systems and machinery. - Ability to communicate, orally and in writing, pertinent information relative to assigned area of technical expertise. - Ability to analyze problems and propose solutions. - Responsiveness to customers and the ability to work well with others. - Ability to become familiar with the ABS Health, Safety, Quality, and Environmental Management Systems.

Physical Requirements:

- Where allowed by local laws, a pre-employment physical examination is mandatory. - The role of surveyor/auditor requires sufficient physical strength, stamina, agility, and both visual and auditory acuity to perform the listed duties effectively. - The ability to climb vertical ladders up to nine meters and navigate steep steps is essential. - Shall be capable of working at heights on various staging and lifting equipment. - Shall be able to maneuver in tight spaces and work inside confined areas for extended periods, including kneeling and crawling. - The role may involve exposure to industrial environments, potential injury risks, extreme weather conditions, and demanding physical activities. - Shall be able to lift at least 25 lbs. / 11.34 kgs. - The use of small tools and the wearing of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), in accordance with ABS safety procedures, may be required. - Where allowed by local laws, the surveyor will be required to successfully complete an annual physical that will recertify the individual can perform the physical actions required.

Reporting Relationships:

Will report to the Principal, Senior, or Surveyor-in-Charge of the assigned port. This position does not have any direct reports.

About Us

We set out more than 160 years ago to promote the security of life and property at sea and preserve the natural environment. Today, we remain true to our mission and continue to support organizations facing a rapidly evolving seascape of challenging regulations and new technologies. Through it all, we are anchored by a vision and mission that help our clients find clarity in uncertain times.

ABS is a global leader in marine and offshore classification and other innovative safety, quality, and environmental services. Weâre at the forefront of supporting the global energy transition at sea, the application of remote and autonomous marine systems, cutting-edge technical solutions, and many more exciting advancements. Our commitment to safety, reliability, and efficiency is ever-present, guiding our clients to safer and more efficient operations.

Equal Opportunity

ABS Bureau is committed to the equal employment opportunity of its employees and prohibits discrimination against any employee or qualified applicant based on race, color, creed, religion, national origin, sex, gender identity, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, citizenship status or veteran status, or other non-work-related characteristics that may be protected under the law of the Federal Government or specific state employment laws.

ABS and Affiliated Companies (ABS) will not pay a fee to any third-party agency without a valid ABS Master Service Agreement (MSA) authorized and signed by Human Resources. Any resume, CV, application, or other forms of candidate submission provided to any employee of ABS without a valid MSA on file will be considered property of ABS, and no fee will be paid.
